bull_bear.body: HEG Limited itself is debt-free with ₹858cr of treasury and has been debt-free for years. Growth capital is going into the electrode expansion (115,000t), and — via the entity that is being demerged — into ₹2,200cr of anode capex (₹1,240cr SBI project debt, rest equity and internal accruals) plus renewable build-out. The Statkraft/Malana buy-in (~₹1,200cr, 50% bank + family office + Bhilwara Energy) leaves ₹600cr in BEL's books that management says will be retired before consolidation. Post-demerger equity structure: ~32.9cr shares in the Greentech entity versus HEG's current ~19.7-19.8cr, with ~13cr new shares to Singularity (both tranches), promoters and RSWM — and management was explicit that **no fresh issuance follows once this is routed**. Treasury is also carrying foreign equity investments whose mark-to-market swings have now materially distorted two consecutive quarters of reported profit in opposite directions.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body:
- **The price-cost lag cuts both ways.** Q1's 29% margin was helped by cheap legacy needle coke; from November-January the $200-300/t increase lands. HEG's own price increases start only in October and management explicitly cannot yet say what average increase it will achieve — "*we'll know in next 1 or 2 months.*" A margin-maintenance promise made before either side of the equation is settled is a genuine risk.
- **Peer price hikes may not stick.** Management pointedly declined to say whether GrafTech's increase is being absorbed: "*How much gets eventually absorbed by the steelmakers, that remains to be seen*". The entire H2 realisation thesis rests on announcements, not on realised prices.
- **US trade action pending, on a compressed clock.** CVD preliminary determination by end-July, anti-dumping by end-September. Exposure is <10% of volume and management is relaxed ("*We know that we have not done dumping*"), but the Chairman also conceded HEG "*might lose some sort of a market share*" in a market where "*American prices are higher than most of the others.*"
- **Structural oversupply is unresolved.** Global UHP demand is contested (an analyst put the market at ~600kt with a third Chinese; management said the Chinese share is "much less, maybe half of that"), Western utilisation sits at 60-65%, and steel industry utilisation is "*even less than 75%.*" The pricing case therefore depends on demand returning and new EAFs commissioning — both outside HEG's control.
- **Anode execution risk is now the dominant company-specific risk.** 60% of ₹2,200cr still to spend, production promised for Q1 FY28, and ~₹1,500cr of gross debt landing on the 31-Mar-27 balance sheet — on a business with no operating history, entering a market dominated by incumbent Chinese suppliers. The mitigant (70% of capacity on 3-5 year Tier-1 contracts) is itself an unconfirmed promise due within six weeks.
- **Reported profit is being distorted by treasury mark-to-market**, in both directions across Q4FY26 and Q1FY27. The "maintain 28-29% including other income" formulation embeds this.
- **Demerger timing is with the NCLT.** The order is reserved but unpronounced; record date, listing mechanics and the ~13cr share issuance all follow from it.
- **Disclosure limits.** Management explicitly refused regional volume splits, specific dollar-per-tonne contracted prices, and net spread economics on competitive-sensitivity grounds — defensible, but it makes the H2 margin promise unverifiable until it is reported.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident, senior and specific where it counts — Riju Jhunjhunwala gave a full three-year revenue and margin build for the anode business unprompted, and Puneet Anand walked through capex phasing, debt quantum and post-demerger share count without hedging. Ravi Jhunjhunwala drew clear lines on competitively sensitive disclosure ("*it is not the right forum… we have competitors all over the world*") rather than giving vague answers, and corrected an analyst's 20% US-exposure figure to 10% directly. There is some looseness: an analyst's question about "BEL debt" was answered as if it referred to HEG's own debt before being clarified as Bhilwara Energy; the anode capex figure moved between ₹2,200cr and ₹2,300cr; and the margin commitment was extracted rather than volunteered. The offer to name individual EAF customer projects offline is a good sign of genuine bottom-up demand tracking rather than citing OECD headlines.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body:
- **The sequential earnings swing is far less dramatic than it looks.** Q4FY26's -₹126cr standalone EBITDA was driven by mark-to-market losses on foreign equity investments; Q1FY27's ₹43cr other income includes fair-valuation *gains* on the same holdings. The underlying operating recovery is real but a fraction of the -₹126cr → +₹211cr headline.
- **Volumes fell and margins expanded 600bps.** In a commodity business that is the most informative fact on the call — it says the electrode cycle has turned on price, not on demand, and that HEG's mix and cost position are doing the work.
- **The needle coke inflation is timed to hit exactly when HEG's own price increases arrive.** Both are Q3 events: HEG's book rolls off in September/October, needle coke cost lands November-January. Q2 should therefore look like Q1; the real test is Q3.
- **HEG's US "risk" is priced backwards.** The US is <10% of volume but carries the highest prices globally — so an adverse ADD/CVD outcome costs disproportionately more margin than volume. The Chairman's "*we will retain America*" reflects that asymmetry.
- **The demerger is being used to house a leveraged growth entity separately from the cash-generative core.** HEG Limited stays debt-free with ₹858cr of treasury; ~₹1,500cr of gross debt, ₹3,100cr of anode capex and the renewable build-out all sit in the entity going out — a clean risk separation that also means post-demerger the listed HEG will look very different from today's consolidated numbers.
- **Anode contracts are being locked in 3-5 year Tier-1 agreements before commissioning** — an unusually strong de-risking of a greenfield battery-materials plant, and the single item most worth verifying next quarter.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- The restructuring enables each entity to raise capital independently for growth, with HEG Greentech to be listed separately.
- Steady hydro cash flows (~â¹300+ Cr annually) are used to self-fund the anode and graphene growth roadmap, supplemented by equity and debt.

business.body:
- **Graphite electrodes (HEG Ltd):** 100,000 TPA at a single location — by far the world's largest, against the next two largest plants at ~70,000 TPA each; expanding to 115,000 TPA by early 2028, widening the scale gap. Running >90%, exports 70-75%, present in 30+ countries. Middle East ~20% of sales; USA <10%.
- **TACC Limited (graphite anode):** 20,000 TPA under construction, ₹2,200-2,300cr capex, 40% spent, commercial production Q1 FY28, ~35% target EBITDA margin, 4-5 year payback; ₹1,240cr SBI debt secured. Phase 2 of 10,000t (~₹800cr) targeted for 2029; land supports 30,000t.
- **Bhilwara Energy (BEL):** two operating hydro plants totalling ~300MW, debt-free, throwing off ₹320-350cr of annual free cash flow. Run-of-river IPPs with 30-40% peaking power sold as high as ₹7-10/unit against ~₹4 for regular power, blending to ~₹5.5+. Statkraft's 49% of Malana Power bought in for ~₹1,200cr. Pipeline: 75MW hydro (~2029) and 300MW DC C&I solar (~18 months), together ~₹200cr incremental EBITDA.
- **HEG Advanced Materials / HEG Greentech:** the demerger vehicle. NCLT order reserved; separate investor call promised on pronouncement. Post-scheme ~32.9cr shares.
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
- **Scale at a single location is the stated cost moat:** 100,000 TPA versus ~70,000 TPA for the next two largest plants globally, going to 115,000 TPA — "*its scale and cost-efficient operations place HEG among the most competitive producers globally*", and the Chairman's blunt claim, "*we will have a higher margin than anybody else.*"
- **Consolidated global industry structure.** "*There are only 3, 4 of us in the world*" outside China, which is why GrafTech's and Tokai's announced increases translate into a sector-wide price move HEG can follow rather than fight.
- **Utilisation gap versus Western peers.** HEG runs >90% while Western capacity utilisation is ~60-65% (per an analyst, uncontested) — evidence that HEG's market access, not capacity, is the binding constraint.
- **Geographic diversification as tariff insurance.** Exports across 30+ countries with no single dominant market means US anti-dumping/countervailing action on <10% of volume is absorbable: "*if something comes, which is totally unreasonable, it will not be difficult for us to absorb that volume elsewhere.*"
- **Balance sheet as an option.** Debt-free with ₹858cr treasury, funding a ₹2,200cr anode programme with only ₹1,240cr of project debt.

business.title: Notable from the deck

latest_quarter.body: Standalone margin of 29% (vs 23% a year ago) on *lower* volumes — the drivers are realisation improvement (~7-8% price improvement in Q1 per a prior media interview), product and geographic mix, and the fact that **old, cheaper needle coke stock is still in the cost base**. That is the crux of the H2 setup: needle coke has risen $200-300/t since the Middle East disruption and adds roughly 10-15% to electrode cost, but 3-4 months of inventory plus a 3-4 month conversion cycle push the impact to November-January. HEG's own price increases start from October as the September/October book rolls off. Management would not quantify the net spread — "*rather than going into the specific number, which is very risky on a call*" — committing only to maintaining current margins. Energy costs and ocean freight are the other inflating inputs; management frames a price increase as an industry necessity rather than an opportunity: "*as an industry, we all need a price increase.*"
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

latest_quarter.body:
- **Q1 FY27 (this):** Standalone revenue ₹681cr (+11% YoY, +13% QoQ), EBITDA ₹211cr / 29% (vs ₹154cr / 23% YoY and **-₹126cr in Q4FY26**), PAT ₹110cr (+53% YoY, vs -₹163cr QoQ); consol EBITDA ₹194cr / 27%, PAT ₹122cr. Volumes *down*; utilisation >90% (91%); entire improvement from realisation, mix and legacy cheap needle coke. Q4's losses and Q1's ₹43cr other income both driven by mark-to-market on foreign equity investments. Debt-free, ₹858cr treasury. Guidance: utilisation 90-95% for FY27 with no headroom above 94-95%; margins to be maintained at ~28-29%; own price increases only from October (peers GrafTech $600-1,200/t, Tokai $930/t announced); needle coke +$200-300/t hits P&L Nov-Jan; 115,000 TPA electrode expansion by early 2028. Anode (TACC): production Q1 FY28, ₹600-700cr year-1 revenue at 40-50% utilisation → >₹1,200cr year 2 → ₹1,500-1,600cr year 3 at ~35% EBITDA margin, 4-5 year payback; 40% of ₹2,200cr capex spent; **70% of capacity to be contracted on 3-5 year Tier-1 deals within 1-1.5 months**; ~₹1,500cr gross debt by 31-Mar-27; phase 2 +10,000t at ₹800cr by 2029. Greentech: 300MW hydro throwing ₹320-350cr FCF, +300MW solar in 18 months, +75MW hydro by ~2029, ~₹200cr incremental EBITDA, **₹1,000cr+ EBITDA targeted by 2030**. Demerger: NCLT order **reserved**; post-scheme ~32.9cr shares.
- _Q2 FY27 → check: **70% of anode capacity contracted** (promised within 1-1.5 months of 24-Jul); NCLT order pronounced and record date announced; US CVD (end-July) and ADD (end-September) outcomes; utilisation staying >90%; margins holding at ~29% before the cost step-up; anode capex burn tracking to 90-95% of ₹2,200cr by end-FY27._
- _Q3 FY27 → the real test: **HEG's own October price increases realised** versus the **needle coke $200-300/t cost landing Nov-Jan**. The margin-maintenance promise is decided here, not in Q2._
latest_quarter.title: QoQ change log (fill each quarter)

outlook.body:
- **Utilisation: >90% in forthcoming quarters, closing FY27 between 90% and 95%** — with an explicit ceiling: "*there's no more headroom beyond 94% or 95%… because then you have to create ideal conditions to reach 100% and conditions are never ideal.*" Chairman's closing line: "*we will produce at 90%, 95% capacity utilisation come what may.*"
- **Margins: maintained at current levels.** Chairman declined a number then confirmed the ~28-29% (including other income) framing when pressed: "*we'll be able to maintain the margins that we are now talking about. And we will have a higher margin than anybody else.*"
- **Pricing: HEG's own increases only take effect from October** — the book is committed through September/October. New business is already being booked at higher prices. Peers have announced **GrafTech $600-1,200/t** (by size/quality) and **Tokai Carbon $930/t**; HEG will "follow suit" but expects nothing substantial in the next one to two quarters because the industry is broadly sold out.
- **Cost lag: needle coke increase of $200-300/t hits the P&L only towards Nov-Dec-Jan**, given 3-4 months of stock plus a 3-4 month conversion cycle. Needle coke is roughly **10-15% of electrode cost**.
- **Electrode capacity: expansion from 100,000 to 115,000 TPA is "on track" and "should be in operation by early 2028."**
- **Anode (TACC) — the most quantified guidance on the call:** commercial production starts **Q1 FY28**; year 1 at 40-50% utilisation → **revenue ₹600-700cr**; year 2 **>₹1,200cr**; year 3 **₹1,500-1,600cr**; **EBITDA margin ~35%** across all three years; **payback 4-5 years** on the ₹2,200cr capex.
- **Anode contracting: ~70% of the 20,000t capacity to be locked into 3-5 year contracts with Tier-1 global players "within the next 1, 1.5 months."**
- **Anode capex phasing:** ₹2,200-2,300cr total for 20,000t; **40% already spent**; 90-95% of payments by end-FY27, balance ~10% in Q1 FY28.
- **Anode phase 2:** a further **10,000t for ~₹800cr, decided immediately after the 20,000t completes, facility up by 2029** (land supports 30,000t). Full 30,000t programme ≈ ₹3,100cr, ~70% debt-financed.
- **TACC debt:** ₹1,240cr already secured from SBI; **~₹1,500cr gross debt expected on the 31-Mar-2027 balance sheet**; balance funded from own capital and internal accruals.
- **Bhilwara Energy / Greentech power:** 300MW of operating hydro, debt-free, generating **₹320-350cr free cash flow per year** at an assumed blended realisation of **~₹5.5/unit**; a **300MW DC C&I solar project in the next 18 months** and a **75MW hydro (acquired from Statkraft, ~30% of work already done) by ~2029 (2.5 years)**, together adding **~₹200cr of EBITDA**.
- **HEG Greentech: "by the year 2030, we should be aiming at a 4-digit EBITDA between all the businesses combined"** (i.e. ₹1,000cr+).
- **Demerger:** NCLT has **reserved its order**; timeline and record date to follow, plus a dedicated investor call on HEG Advanced Materials once pronounced. Post-scheme share count in the demerged entity ~**32.9cr shares** (from HEG's current ~19.7-19.8cr), with ~13cr new shares to Singularity, promoters and RSWM; **no further issuance thereafter**.
- **Malana/Statkraft acquisition debt** (~₹1,200cr paid, 50% commercial banks + family office + Bhilwara Energy; ₹600cr sitting in BEL's books via subsidiaries) to be **retired before the Greentech consolidation**.
outlook.title: Guidance (CRITICAL — verify next quarter)

outlook.body: Electrodes are sold on a rolling 3-4 month forward book — "*normally, we are always booked 3, 4 months ahead*" — currently committed through September/October, which is precisely why announced price increases cannot show up before Q3. Demand pipeline is framed structurally rather than as backlog: OECD counts **~71Mt of new EAF steelmaking capacity planned globally for completion between now and end-2028**; management's own tracking says ~20-21Mt came up across CY24-25, ~**60Mt is due across CY26-28**, of which **8-10Mt landed in H1 CY26**, and offered to name the individual customer projects offline. For the anode business, ~70% of 20,000t capacity is being placed on 3-5 year Tier-1 contracts within six weeks of the call.
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: The graphite-anode business is the genuine second act — a ₹600-700cr revenue business in year one scaling to ₹1,500-1,600cr by year three at ~35% EBITDA margin, contracted 70% forward on 3-5 year Tier-1 agreements before the plant even runs. Beyond that, the green-energy stack (300MW hydro today, +75MW hydro and +300MW solar) is being assembled into an entity targeting ₹1,000cr+ of EBITDA by 2030. On the core, the 115,000t electrode expansion plus CBAM-driven EAF conversion is the long-cycle option: management pointedly notes that **no new blast furnace is coming up in Europe or the US** — all incremental steel capacity there is electric arc.
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis: A violent sequential swing back to profit — standalone EBITDA from a **-₹126cr loss in Q4FY26 to +₹211cr**, PAT from -₹163cr to +₹110cr — achieved on *lower* volumes, entirely through realisation and mix, with margins at 29% standalone. The forward setup is unusually legible: GrafTech and Tokai have announced electrode price hikes of $600-1,200/t and $930/t respectively, HEG is booked through September/October so its own increases only bite from October, and needle coke (up $200-300/t) only hits the P&L in Nov-Jan — a favourable price-cost lag into H2. Underneath, the group is splitting: the graphite-electrode business stays, while **HEG Greentech** (20,000t anode plant commissioning Q1FY28 at ~35% target EBITDA margin, plus 300MW of operating hydro) demerges pending an NCLT order that is already reserved, with management aiming at a **four-digit (₹1,000cr+) EBITDA for Greentech by 2030**.
